## Dispatch order — R34

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`. Branch: **`claude/issue-6392-vestigial-pnpm-steps`**. Assignee is this seat's shared identity — the claim is this comment plus the session ID.

### The ruling you are executing (triage, verbatim across its two comments)

> Charter on unlock is the body's own bounded cut: remove the two pnpm lines (`corepack enable` + `pnpm --version`) from `dependabot-auto-merge.yml` **or** keep `pnpm --version` as a deliberate fail-fast — either way the reasoning gets recorded in the file, per the body's warning that an unexplained removal is how it gets re-added. `actions/setup-node` stays (the merge-gate is a node step); the `cache: 'pnpm'` comment gets re-read, not reflex-deleted. Family: #6391 (same mechanism family, also blocked on #6389) — fold-or-serial at claim time; folding both into one PR post-#6389 likely passes all five family-dispatch doors.

> Unlock (same triage round, corrected): PR #6389 **merged at 19:48Z** — minutes before the grading comment above was written, so the block was stale on arrival. Premise re-verified on the merged PR itself: the driver step at `:105–110` is gone and the `corepack enable` + `pnpm --version` lines remain … `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`.

⛔ **The fold with #6391 is declined by this seat** — one card per agent. **#6391 is out of scope for you**; do not touch `changeset-release.yml`, the `.gitattributes` line, or the "Lockfile Merge Driver" table's remaining row.

### Re-verify the premise on `main` before you cut anything

Triage re-verified on the merged PR; ⚠️ **you verify on `main` at your own HEAD**. Confirm both halves:
1. the driver step (`git config merge.pnpm-merge.name` / `.driver`) is **gone** from `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml`;
2. `corepack enable` and `pnpm --version` (`:91–95`, line numbers certainly shifted) are **still there**.

⛔ If either is false, stop and report — the card's premise is the merge, and a premise that moved is not something to work around.

### The decision is yours, and both answers are legitimate

**Cut both**, or **keep `pnpm --version` as a deliberate fail-fast** — the card argues it proves corepack actually activated, so a later pnpm dependency fails clearly rather than confusingly. Weigh it and choose.

⛔ **Whichever you choose, the reasoning goes in the file.** That is the whole point: the card's own warning is that *an unexplained removal is how it gets re-added*. A silent cut recreates the condition that produced the residue.

### Two things to leave alone, stated so you do not tidy them

- **`actions/setup-node` stays.** `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` is a `node` step and needs a runtime. ⛔ This card is only about the two pnpm lines.
- **The `cache: 'pnpm'` comment gets re-read, not reflex-deleted.** It documents a real failure mode — without a pnpm store, `setup-node`'s post-job cache save fails with a Path Validation Error and marks the whole job failed. ⚠️ If the pnpm steps go, that comment may need rewording rather than removing; it is still the right warning for the next person who reaches for the cache option.

### Constraints

- ⛔ **Worktree-first**: `git worktree add ../objectui-6392 -b claude/issue-6392-vestigial-pnpm-steps main && cd ../objectui-6392 && pnpm install`.
- ⛔ **Never `git stash`** — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo.
- ⛔ **Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.**
- ⛔ Do not set `domain:*` or type labels; file findings **unassigned**.
- ⚠️ If a doc table or pin names this workflow's steps, both halves ship together — `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` pins that page against `.github/workflows/` in **both** directions, and it has turned three PRs red today. **Run the whole `scripts/__tests__` tree**, not a subset: this pin fires on the page as a whole, so a subset chosen from your own subject matter can miss it.
- Changeset required. Open the PR as **draft**; this seat arms it.

### Reporting

Structured JSON report: the re-verified premise with commands, which option you chose **and the reasoning you wrote into the file**, what you did with the `cache: 'pnpm'` comment, and the full-tree test counts.

## Review — ACCEPT (PR #6423)

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R34. Read the diff.

### The charter's real requirement was the comment, and it is the best part of the diff

Either option was legitimate; ⛔ what was not optional was recording the reasoning in the file, because *"an unexplained removal is how it gets re-added."* The note does three things, and the third is the one I would have missed asking for:

1. names what was removed and **when**, and which card removed its only consumer;
2. ⭐ records the **rejected** alternative with its reasoning — *"Considered and rejected: keeping `pnpm --version` alone as a 'proves corepack activated' fail-fast … Rejected because that failure mode has no occasion to matter until something in this job actually calls pnpm"*. A future reader who has that idea finds it already answered;
3. ⭐ gives an **escape hatch with a location**: *"If a future step here grows a real pnpm dependency, add `corepack enable` back next to that step, where a reader can see what it's for."* That is what converts "do not re-add this" into "here is how to re-add it correctly" — the difference between a prohibition and a maintainable one.

⭐ It also now sits directly above #6369's *"No lockfile merge driver here, deliberately"* note. Two adjacent deliberately-absent notes with their reasons is a coherent pattern for this file, not clutter.

### The `cache: 'pnpm'` comment was reworded, not deleted — and the tense was fixed

It keeps the Path Validation Error warning intact (still the right warning for the next person reaching for that option) and adds *"this job doesn't set up pnpm at all."* ⚠️ Note the tense change from *"fails"* to *"would fail"* — correct now that there is no pnpm setup to trigger it. That is the kind of detail a reflex delete-or-keep decision loses.

### The verification I most wanted, and did not ask for

> Re-parsed the edited YAML with `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` and printed the job's step list to confirm exactly the two pnpm steps are gone and every other step … is unchanged.

⭐ A YAML edit that removes two steps is exactly where an indentation slip silently reparents or drops a neighbour, and no test in this repo would necessarily catch it. Structural re-parse beats reading the diff.

⭐ And the cross-check has a control: `grep -rn "Enable Corepack|Verify pnpm version" .github/workflows/` shows `dependabot-auto-merge.yml` no longer in the list **while twelve workflows that genuinely run `pnpm install` are untouched**. That distinguishes "removed from the right file" from "removed from too many".

Premise re-verified on `main` at its own HEAD with both greps before any edit, as ordered — driver gone, the two lines still present. `git diff --stat`: one workflow plus the changeset, nothing swept in.

### Disposition

⛔ Arming on **every** check green. CI running on the branch head; eight outstanding, no failures. Arms when clean.
